Maize Image Segmentation using Watershed

Contents

  • Steps:
  • Step 1: Load the image
  • Step 2: Preprocess the image
  • Step 3: Threshold and compute distance transform
  • Step 4: Detect seed points (local maxima)
  • Step 5: Apply Watershed segmentation
  • Step 6: Visualize the result using a curtain
This notebook may contain text, code and images generated by artificial intelligence. Used model: claude-sonnet-4-6, vision model: claude-sonnet-4-6, fast_model: None, endpoint: None, bia-bob version: 0.36.2.. It is good scientific practice to check the code and results it produces carefully. Read more about code generation using bia-bob

Maize Image Segmentation using Watershed#

This notebook segments dark objects (cells) between bright membranes in a maize microscopy image using the Watershed algorithm.

Steps:#

  1. Load the image data/maize.tif

  2. Preprocess the image (Gaussian blur + invert) to prepare for watershed

  3. Compute distance transform or use inverted image as topography

  4. Find seed points (local maxima in the dark regions)

  5. Apply the Watershed algorithm

  6. Visualize the result using a curtain

import numpy as np
import stackview
from skimage.io import imread
from skimage.filters import gaussian, threshold_otsu
from skimage.segmentation import watershed
from skimage.feature import peak_local_max
from scipy.ndimage import label as ndi_label
from scipy.ndimage import distance_transform_edt

Step 1: Load the image#

image = imread('data/maize.tif')

stackview.insight(image)
shape(640, 639)
dtypeuint8
size399.4 kB
min0
max255

Step 2: Preprocess the image#

We apply a Gaussian blur to reduce noise, then invert the image so that dark cell interiors become bright regions, which are suitable for distance transform and seed detection.

blurred = gaussian(image.astype(float), sigma=2)
inverted = blurred.max() - blurred

stackview.insight(inverted)
shape(640, 639)
dtypefloat64
size3.1 MB
min0.0
max233.3670744062649

Step 3: Threshold and compute distance transform#

We threshold the inverted image to create a binary mask of the cell regions, then compute a distance transform to find the centers of the cells.

thresh = threshold_otsu(inverted)
binary = inverted > thresh
distance = distance_transform_edt(binary)

stackview.insight(distance)
shape(640, 639)
dtypefloat64
size3.1 MB
min0.0
max86.4060183089118

Step 4: Detect seed points (local maxima)#

We detect local maxima in the distance map to use as seeds for the watershed algorithm.

coords = peak_local_max(distance, min_distance=10, labels=binary)
mask = np.zeros(distance.shape, dtype=bool)
mask[tuple(coords.T)] = True
markers, _ = ndi_label(mask)

print(f'Number of seeds detected: {markers.max()}')

Number of seeds detected: 234

Step 5: Apply Watershed segmentation#

We apply the watershed algorithm using the negative distance map as the topography and the detected seeds as markers, masked to the binary cell regions.

labels = watershed(-distance, markers, mask=binary)

stackview.insight(labels)
shape(640, 639)
dtypeint32
size1.6 MB
min0
max234
n labels234

Step 6: Visualize the result using a curtain#

We overlay the segmentation label image on top of the original image using an interactive curtain for comparison.

stackview.curtain(image, labels)

stackview.animate_curtain(image, labels, filename="maize_curtain.gif")
